title: Symphony No. 40 in G minor
hook: Classical elegance with a racing pulse underneath.

painting.title: A Shipwreck in Stormy Seas
painting.pairingNote: The same years, the same taste for storm and agitation held inside a perfectly balanced frame.

facts: Written in the summer of 1788, within about six weeks, alongside Symphonies No. 39 and No. 41. They were Mozart’s last three.
One of only two symphonies Mozart wrote in a minor key. Both are in G minor.
There are no trumpets and no drums. All the drama comes from strings and woodwinds.
Mozart later added clarinets to the score, which suggests the work was performed in his lifetime.
bigPicture.inOneLine: anxiety in motion (I), an uneasy calm (II), a stern dance (III), a race that refuses a happy ending (IV).

movements.heading: Molto allegro
movements.summary: The symphony starts as if we had walked in on something already under way: a murmuring accompaniment first, then one of the most famous tunes in music. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]].

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, agitation
mainIdeas.description: a sighing three-note figure (short, short, long) repeated in the violins over restless violas.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, brief relief
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, sliding melody shared between strings and woodwinds, in a [[major|major]] key.

stops.hear: Violas murmur for a moment alone; then violins enter with the sighing tune
stops.happening: Theme 1. The accompaniment begins before the melody, which was highly unusual

stops.hear: A pause, then a softer melody passed between strings and woodwinds
stops.happening: Theme 2, in B-flat major. The only calm in the movement

stops.hear: The opening returns exactly
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] is repeated

stops.hear: The sighing tune appears in a strange, distant key, then is tossed between low and high strings
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The theme is pulled apart until only its three-note sigh remains

stops.hear: Woodwinds drift downward and the sighing tune slips back in
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The gentle second melody returns, but darker
stops.happening: Theme 2 is now in G minor. The relief it offered earlier is withdrawn

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A last quiet statement of the sigh, then firm chords
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: The whole first theme grows out of three notes. Count how often you hear that short-short-long rhythm.
Compare Theme 2 the first time (major, consoling) with its return (minor, resigned). Same notes, opposite effect.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: The only movement that leaves G minor. It sounds calm, but the calm is built from nervous little pieces.

mainIdeas.description: A theme made of repeated notes that enters one layer at a time: violas, second violins, first violins.
Tiny two-note flutters that flicker through strings and woodwinds.

stops.hear: Repeated notes stacking up from low to high
stops.happening: The main theme assembles itself in layers

stops.hear: Quick two-note flutters, like small sighs, passing between instruments
stops.happening: The second idea. It will decorate everything from here on

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: The repeated notes turn insistent and the harmony darkens
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The calm surface cracks

stops.hear: The layered opening returns
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

notice: The flutter figure is a cousin of the sigh from the first movement.

movements.heading: Menuetto: Allegretto
movements.summary: A [[minuet|minuet]] in name only. Nobody could dance to this: it is stern, angular and full of clashing lines.

stops.hear: A heavy, striding tune with accents in unexpected places
stops.happening: The minuet. Phrases are three bars long instead of the usual four, which keeps it off balance

stops.hear: Upper and lower instruments chase each other with the same tune
stops.happening: The lines overlap in [[canon|canon]], grinding against each other

stops.hear: Suddenly gentle: strings, then woodwinds, then glowing horns
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], in G major. The most peaceful minute of the symphony

stops.hear: The stern dance returns
stops.happening: The minuet is repeated

movements.heading: Allegro assai
movements.summary: A fast, driven finale in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] that stays in the minor to the last bar.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quiet upward leap through a chord, answered by a loud outburst.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a smooth, singing line in the violins.

stops.hear: Soft rising figure, loud answer, soft, loud
stops.happening: Theme 1. A question-and-answer built on an upward [[arpeggio|arpeggio]]

stops.hear: A calmer, singing melody in the violins, echoed by clarinet
stops.happening: Theme 2, in B-flat major

stops.hear: A jagged, stumbling passage for the whole orchestra with no clear key
stops.happening: The start of the [[development|development]]. For a few seconds Mozart touches almost every note of the scale and the music loses its footing

stops.hear: The rising figure piled on top of itself, entering in one section after another
stops.happening: A stretch of [[fugato|fugato]]

stops.hear: The quiet rising figure returns
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The singing melody again, now in the minor; then a brisk close
stops.happening: No turn to the major. The symphony ends as darkly as it began

notice: That jagged passage at the start of the development is one of the strangest moments in 18th-century music. It lasts only a few seconds.

threads.title: The minor key holds
threads.body: Three of four movements are in G minor, and the finale refuses the customary happy ending.

threads.title: Sighs
threads.body: Short falling figures run through the first, second and last movements.

threads.title: Drama without drums
threads.body: With no trumpets or timpani, the tension comes from harmony and rhythm alone.
